title: When Smart pen (Wacom) has low battery, notification about it appears every time when you draw with it
line: A stylus or other peripheral with a low battery now warns once, not again every time it comes back into range.
explanation: A pen's battery shows up in UPower only while the pen is near the tablet, so it is added and removed all the time. PowerDevil treated every addition as a new device and compared its charge against a made-up 'previous' value of 1000, so a low pen got a fresh 'Device Battery Low' notification every time it came into range. The change remembers each peripheral's last known charge by vendor, model and serial (its UDI can change) and uses it as the previous value when the device comes back, so it only warns again after the battery was above the low level in between.

commits.message:
daemon: don't warn again about a low peripheral battery that comes back

A stylus disappears and reappears as it leaves and enters the tablet's
range, and each time it came back with a low battery a new warning was
shown. Remember each device's last charge, warn only when it gets low.

BUG: 527371

media.caption: Pure master: the pen (6%) comes into range three times; each time a new 'Device Battery Low' notification pops up.
With the fix: same three appearances; only the first shows the warning, the tray still counts 1 unread notification.
Video of the three appearances on master: three notifications.
Video of the same steps with the fix: one notification.

reviews.text: Good root-cause diagnosis and valid direction to deduplicate low-battery warnings for peripherals that frequently disconnect and reconnect, with clear dbusmock verification. However, recording m_lastPeripheralBatteriesPercent unconditionally in onDeviceAdded() and onDeviceRemoved() suppresses the first warning whenever a low peripheral was previously seen while !m_notificationsReady, !b->isPresent(), or Battery::Charging, and the unseparated vendor+product+serial key can collide when fields are empty.
changes: Only record a peripheral as already warned when emitBatteryChargePercentNotification() actually emits a notification (and reset that state when charge rises above peripheralBatteryLowLevel()), so a device previously seen while !m_notificationsReady, !isPresent(), or charging does not silently suppress its first real low-battery warning.

Use a delimited identity key (or structured key) for vendor/product/serial and fall back to UDI (or skip cross-UDI deduplication) when all three fields are empty so nameless peripherals do not collide.

In Core::onDeviceRemoved(), guard the m_peripheralBatteryIds lookup explicitly (e.g. via find()/contains()) rather than relying on m_peripheralBatteriesPercent.value(udi) > 0 to skip non-peripheral batteries.

reviews.text: Right cause and layer: onDeviceAdded() passed a fake previous value of 1000 for every peripheral, so a pen whose UPower battery is re-created on proximity (as the wacom driver does) got a fresh 'normal->low' warning each time. Remembering the last charge per vendor+product+serial (UDIs get renumbered) and feeding it as previousPercent keeps the existing 'once per normal->low transition' rule intact across re-adds, which matches Nate's 'once per login or so' and the reporter's complaint. The before/after screenshots and video show three warnings vs one, and the regression list covers UDI renumbering, a different device, recharge-then-low, live drop and daemon restart. Nit: devices without a serial share an entry, which is documented and harmless.
